Thanks Alice — great questions. I pulled together a short integration note below and attached a one-page observability playbook and SDK quickstart. Long form doc is on the drive link Marissa shared.

Integration + architecture notes (high level):
- SDK setup:
  - We provide official SDKs (Python, Node) and a simple REST fallback. Quickstart in attached redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf.
  - Example (pseudo):
    const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west' });

- Auth patterns:
  - PoC: API keys with short TTL and built-in rotation helpers in the SDK.
  - Prod options: mTLS or IAM-backed tokens for Dedicated/Private.

- Routing / topology:
  - Recommend two routes: low-latency route for chat (pinned model, small batch) and high-throughput route for batch embeddings (larger batch sizes, async).
  - Use our route header X-Redwood-Route: chat|embeddings to control placement.

- Structured output / tool-calling:
  - SDK supports function/tool calling with a structured JSON envelope. We can optionally return a telemetry object when structured output is enabled: {"telemetry": {...}} (see playbook).

- Embeddings / reranker guidance:
  - For 200k records, start with batched embedding requests (batch size 256-1024 depending on payload size).
  - Typical throughput: 2-3k embeddings/sec on a dedicated pool per GPU (quantized models vary). We'll provide a recommended quantization profile for your corpus.

Observability hooks (specifics you can implement today):
- Trace propagation: accept standard W3C traceparent and return X-Redwood-Trace-Id in responses. We also echo incoming trace_id into our logs for cross-correlation.
- Response headers (examples):
  - X-Redwood-Trace-Id: <uuid>
  - X-Redwood-Queue-ms: <integer> (time spent queued before execution)
  - X-Redwood-Infer-ms: <integer> (model inference time)
  - X-Redwood-Total-ms: <integer> (end-to-end request time)
- Structured telemetry: when using structured output you can request telemetry=true and get telemetry fields in the JSON payload (trace_id, token_count, latency_breakdown).
- Logging fields: we write: trace_id, request_id, model_version, region, route, user_id (when provided). These fields are available in the log export (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/S3).
- Sampling: default is head-based sampling for traces on our Hosted plan; we can configure 100% sampling for early integration/testing upon request.

Attachments: I've attached the redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf and observability_playbook.md. Also added a short dashboard template (Drive link).

If you want, we can run a short 90-min workshop with your SRE to wire up trace propagation and test headers.
